text:
Continuous integration, or CI, is a software development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a central repository. Each time code is committed, an automated build is triggered. This build compiles the new code and then runs a series of tests to check for errors.

The main goal of CI is to catch issues early. Instead of discovering problems after weeks of work, developers are alerted within minutes if a change breaks something. This is made possible through CI pipelines, which are automated sequences of steps. By fixing bugs right away, teams save time, improve code quality, and reduce the risk of major failures.
